accepted.label: Excel Data Model basics
accepted.description: The Excel Data Model is a feature that lets you combine multiple tables into a single pivot table by creating relationships. It is activated by adding tables to the model when creating a pivot table.
coverage_criteria: Explain what the Excel Data Model is used for.
Demonstrate how to add tables to the Data Model when creating a PivotTable.
accepted.merge_rationale: Both candidates describe the foundational purpose and the key step to use the Data Model, forming one teachable concept.

accepted.label: Creating relationships in the Excel Data Model
accepted.description: Excel can automatically detect relationships between tables based on matching field names or values, or users can manually create them via the Relationships dialog. Using consistent field names facilitates automatic detection.
coverage_criteria: Explain how Excel can automatically detect relationships.
Describe how to manually create a relationship in the Data Model.
State the importance of consistent field naming for relationship detection.
accepted.merge_rationale: These candidates cover different aspects of establishing relationships: auto-detection, manual creation, and a best practice tip, which together form a unified topic.
